critical.issue: Returns HTTP 500 {detail:'EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY missing or invalid'} instead of {status:'pending', detail:...} when placeholder key is set. Root cause: in server.py register_push() the 401-branch raises HTTPException(500), then the outer 'except HTTPException: raise' propagates the 500 to the client, bypassing the intended graceful fallback (which lives in the generic Exception branch). Per task spec, placeholder key must NOT cause a 5xx — frontend onMount calls registerForPush() and a 500 will surface as an unhandled rejection. Fix: in the 401 branch, return {'status': 'pending', 'detail': 'Push key not configured'} (or fall through to the generic except by raising a non-HTTPException).

First-time call returns 500 with TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable") (seen in backend logs from real user 620f4d38-...). Root cause: when prefs doc doesn't exist, code builds `defaults = NotifPrefs(user_id=user_id).dict()`, then calls `db.notif_prefs.insert_one(defaults)` which MUTATES defaults in-place adding the new ObjectId `_id`, then `return defaults` includes _id and FastAPI fails to serialize. Fix: either pop '_id' before returning, or pass a copy to insert_one, or use a projection round-trip.

minor.issue: Same 401-on-placeholder pattern exists in send_push() — but notifications_test wraps it in try/except and returns {status:'pending'} correctly. Behaviour is OK; just noting the duplicate 401-raise-500 pattern shared with register-push.

rca_of_issue: Bug 1 (register-push 500): server.py lines 456-459 explicitly raise HTTPException(500) and HTTPException(502) inside the try block, then lines 461-462 'except HTTPException: raise' re-raise them as-is. The graceful pending fallback only triggers for non-HTTP exceptions (network errors, JSON decode errors). Since placeholder key cleanly returns 401 from upstream, the 500 path always fires. Reproduction: POST /api/register-push with any body — observe 500. Mitigation: convert the 401 branch from `raise HTTPException(500, ...)` to `return {'status': 'pending', 'detail': 'Push key not configured'}`. Bug 2 (notif-prefs ObjectId leak): pymotor's insert_one mutates the passed dict in-place to insert an ObjectId at key '_id' on success. The defaults dict is then returned directly, leaking ObjectId into the FastAPI serializer which cannot encode it. Reproduction: hit GET /api/notif-prefs/<any-new-uuid> — first call 500, subsequent calls 200 (because the doc now exists and find_one has projection {'_id':0}). Mitigation: defaults.pop('_id', None) after insert_one, or insert_one(dict(defaults)).
